_note: One tip is shown per day on the homepage, rotating. Add or edit freely.
tips: Register on Udyam first. It is free, takes minutes on udyamregistration.gov.in, and nearly every MSME scheme asks for it.
Government schemes are free to apply. Anyone asking for a fee to ‘guarantee’ approval is a red flag — apply on the official portal.
PMEGP, CMEGP and state margin-money schemes generally can’t be combined for the same unit. Pick the one that pays the most for your project size.
A collateral-free loan is usually CGTMSE-backed. Ask your bank branch to process it ‘under CGTMSE’ by name.
Your project report decides most loan files. Show realistic sales, costs and a repayment plan — not optimistic guesses.
Women, SC/ST, ex-servicemen and divyang applicants get higher subsidy rates under PMEGP and CMEGP. Keep your category certificate ready.
Public sector bank branches process most scheme-linked loans. Ask for the branch’s MSME or scheme nodal officer.
Keep GST, bank statements and ITRs in order for 12 months before applying — banks check them even for subsidy-linked loans.
Startup? Get DPIIT recognition first — it is free and unlocks the Seed Fund, tax benefits and easier compliance.
Check your district’s ODOP product in UP — units making it get priority under margin-money and marketing support.
Subsidies are often credited to the loan account after a lock-in period. Plan cash flow as if the subsidy arrives later.
State incentives often depend on location (taluka or zone). The same factory can earn very different subsidies a few kilometres apart.
Ask for the sanction letter in writing and keep copies of every submission and acknowledgement number.
Mudra has four tiers — Shishu, Kishore, Tarun and Tarun Plus. Apply for the tier that matches your real need, not the maximum.
Exporters: check PLI and NSIC support before expanding capacity — some incentives need you to apply before you invest.
